note: Item text is each source column's own header in the five S1-S5 XLS files (columns '11:I feel more nervous or anxious than usual' .. '30:I had nightmares', identical and in the same order in all five files), with only the leading 'NN:' questionnaire number stripped; no other normalisation (casing, apostrophes, 'pee', 'I think I might be going crazy' kept as printed). Option text is the label each source cell carries before its score, e.g. 'considerable time(3.0)': 'No or little time', 'a small portion of time', 'considerable time', 'Most or all of the time' (source casing kept). CODE DERIVATION IS POSITIONAL: the script filters columns numbered 11-30 and renames the i-th to sas_i, so Step 5b is owed despite mapping_basis=data_labels; verify_shen_2020_sas20.R reproduces all 80 item x resp counts from the raw files against a server-side GROUP BY of the live table (each live item matches exactly one header column, its own), and diffs item_text 20/20 and option_text 80/80 against the source. RESP IS STORED ALREADY REVERSE-SCORED for items 5, 9, 13, 17, 19 (sas_5 'I think everything is fine', sas_9, sas_13, sas_17, sas_19), as the paper states ('The items 5, 9, 13, 17 and 19 were reverse scores') and as the source cells encode ('Most or all of the time(1.0)'); so for those five items option_text runs Most or all of the time=1 .. No or little time=4, and for the other 15 No or little time=1 .. Most or all of the time=4. Every label maps to exactly one score within each item across all 1647 rows. Raw-file total score mean 30.85 SD 6.89 (n=1647) reproduces the paper's abstract 30.85 +/- 6.89 exactly (the paper says n=1637; the deposit and live table hold 1647 respondents, and the published statistic matches the 1647). LANGUAGE / FALLBACK: the survey was administered electronically to hospital staff in Zhejiang, China; the deposit's English headers are the authors' rendering, and free-text cells still hold Chinese (Age answers '31岁', '55周岁'; Occupation '其他(0.0)'), confirming a Chinese administration. Administered Chinese item wording not recoverable within scope: checked all five S1-S5 XLS files (zero CJK characters in any header or in any of the 20 SAS columns' 32,940 cells; CJK only in the Age and Occupation columns) and the paper XML (no questionnaire text, no instructions). The paper has no other supplements. So English ships in the base fields with language=Chinese and empty _translated columns; translation_source=study_supplied. The English is NOT canonical Zung (1971) wording (e.g. item 4 'I think I might be going crazy' vs canonical 'I feel like I'm falling apart and going to pieces'); it is a back-rendering of the Chinese SAS, shipped as the study supplied it. No instructions text published; instructions blank. RIGHTS: no rights-register row for the Zung SAS. No quotable restriction located: web search surfaced only third-party statements that the 1971 Psychosomatics scale is treated as public domain; Mapi ePROVIDE's instrument page (eprovide.mapi-trust.org/instruments/zung-self-rating-anxiety-scale) is JS-rendered and returned no terms text. Shipped on silence-is-permission; wording comes from the study's own CC BY 4.0 deposit. No register row written (rounds may not write ship rows) - flagging for the human register. Item codes are positional sas_i, so the wording is not otherwise present in the response table.
public_note: Responses for items sas_5, sas_9, sas_13, sas_17 and sas_19 are stored already reverse-scored, so their option text runs from 'Most or all of the time' (1) to 'No or little time' (4); the English item wording is the study's own rendering of the Chinese SAS it administered, not the original Zung wording.
